task.description: Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0400, per WF-03. ISS-0400's own record (docs/issues/ISS-0400.yaml) already names the affected function (Letflow.Engine.Transition.collect_leaf_gateways/3), the affected file, and the mechanism (a PARALLEL_GATEWAY node is currently always treated as an immediate terminal leaf during the Tarjan-SCC memoized DFS walk, which is correct for the outer split's own join search but means a genuinely nested PARALLEL_GATEWAY split/join pair inside one branch of an outer split cannot be resolved -- the outer find_matching_join/2 call has no way to first resolve the inner pair and treat its result as a single leaf). Do not take that description as sufficient on its own (No Speculation, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1): reproduce the failure directly -- construct or locate a graph fixture with a PARALLEL_GATEWAY nested inside one branch of an outer PARALLEL_GATEWAY split (before that branch reaches the outer join), run it through the current collect_leaf_gateways/3 / find_matching_join/2 path, and confirm the actual failure mode (which error, or which silent-wrong-answer, results) rather than assuming the yaml's prose is exactly right. Then produce a root-cause diagnosis: which function needs to change, what invariant is missing, and what shape a fix needs (e.g. does the outer walk need to recursively resolve an inner split/join pair before treating its result as one leaf, and if so what does 'resolve' mean precisely -- a recursive call to the same join-finding logic, scoped to the inner PARALLEL_GATEWAY's own reachable subgraph). Do NOT implement the fix. Step 0.5: also check docs/issues/*.yaml for any other resolved entry describing the same or a closely related symptom (ISS-0398 itself is the obvious related entry, already linked -- read its own resolution and design doc so the diagnosis doesn't duplicate work) before writing the diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: The failure is reproduced directly against real code (a real test run or repro script quoting real output), not inferred from ISS-0400.yaml's prose alone
Root cause is stated in terms of the specific function(s) and the specific missing invariant/logic gap, not a restatement of the symptom
The diagnosis states what shape a fix needs to take, without writing implementation code
docs/issues/*.yaml resolved entries were checked for a prior match before concluding this is a new root cause
result.next_action names CODE-DESIGNER as the next step

result.summary:
Step 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for nested-PARALLEL_GATEWAY symptoms -- only 2 hits, ISS-0398.yaml (already read in full, cited as ISS-0400's own origin) and ISS-0400.yaml itself. No other resolved entry describes this symptom; ISS-0398's own resolution explicitly named this exact case as out of scope rather than silently leaving it broken, so this is a genuinely new root cause, not a recurrence -- severity stays MINOR, not escalated.

Step 1 (diagnose), reproduced directly against real code, not inferred from ISS-0400.yaml's prose. Two throwaway scripts (run via `MIX_ENV=test mix run <path>`, deleted after use -- scratch/ is git-ignored, nothing under lib/ or test/ was touched):

Repro 1 -- outer_split (PARALLEL_GATEWAY) with 2 branches: branch 0 is the zero-hop control (outer_split -> outer_join directly); branch 1 is outer_split -> pre -> inner_split (PARALLEL_GATEWAY, nested) -> {inner_a, inner_b} -> inner_join (PARALLEL_GATEWAY) -> post -> outer_join -> e. This is exactly ISS-0400's case: a genuinely nested split/join pair, fully resolvable on its own, inside one branch of an outer split, before that branch reaches the outer join. Actual observed output: `Transition.transition(g, state, {:advance_token, "t1"})` returns `{:error, {:no_matching_join_found, "outer_split"}}` -- a hard failure (Engine.create/2's own {:activation_failed, {:no_matching_join_found, split_node_id}} path), not a silent wrong answer.

Repro 2 -- isolated branch 1 alone (outer_split's other edge points at a plain :END 'dead' node instead of outer_join, so cross-branch disagreement can't be attributed to a coincidence with a second real branch): same {:error, {:no_matching_join_found, "outer_split"}} result, confirming branch 1's own collect_leaf_gateways/3 walk independently fails to resolve to outer_join regardless of what the sibling branch does.

ROOT CAUSE, traced against lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's actual source (not assumed from the design doc's prose): collect_leaf_gateways/3's step 4 (transition.ex:934-936, `%Node{node_type: :PARALLEL_GATEWAY} -> leaves = MapSet.new([{:gateway, node_id}]); {:finished, leaves, put_leaf_memo(state, node_id, leaves)}`) treats ANY node whose node_type is :PARALLEL_GATEWAY as an immediate terminal leaf, unconditionally -- it returns `{:gateway, node_id}` and stops, without ever looking at that node's own outgoing edges. This clause cannot distinguish 'this PARALLEL_GATEWAY is the branch's real join' from 'this PARALLEL_GATEWAY is a nested split that itself needs resolving before the walk can continue' -- both shapes hit the exact same pattern match. So in repro 1/2, the walk down branch 1 reaches inner_split, immediately reports leaves = #{{:gateway, "inner_split"}}, and never traverses inner_split's own out-edges to inner_a/inner_b, never reaches inner_join, and never reaches outer_join. find_matching_join/2's per-branch singleton check (transition.ex:826-836) then sees branch 1 resolve to "inner_split" while branch 0 resolves to "outer_join" (repro 1) or branch 1's own value simply isn't {:gateway, "outer_join"} at all (repro 2, where 'dead_end' vs '{:gateway,"inner_split"}' already disagree) -- either way `{:halt, {:error, :no_matching_join}}` fires (transition.ex:831) and dispatch_parallel_split/4 (transition.ex:772-774) surfaces `{:error, {:no_matching_join_found, node.id}}`.

This is precisely the boundary the ISS-0398 design doc names at lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md §2.3: '...does NOT support -- and does not change today's behavior for -- a branch containing a nested PARALLEL_GATEWAY split anywhere along any of its paths.' §4's SECC-closure memoization machinery (Tarjan SCC, index/lowlink/stack) is entirely orthogonal to this defect -- it governs *how many times* a node gets computed under cycles/reconvergence, not *which node types* get treated as terminal, so nothing about §2.2's memoization scheme needs to change. The existing test suite (test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs) does not catch this because none of its fixtures nest a PARALLEL_GATEWAY inside a branch -- every existing fixture's branches pass only through :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY/:HUMAN_TASK nodes before reaching their (single, non-nested) PARALLEL_GATEWAY join.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE (diagnosis only -- no implementation code written, per WF-03 Step 1's own prohibition): collect_leaf_gateways/3's step 4 needs to stop treating every :PARALLEL_GATEWAY node as unconditionally terminal. It must instead distinguish 'this IS the branch's own join' (still terminal, still returns {:gateway, node_id} immediately -- this is what makes the outer find_matching_join/2 call work at all) from 'this is a DIFFERENT, nested split that must itself be resolved first' -- and for the latter case, recursively invoke the same join-finding logic (a call shaped like find_matching_join/2, or an inlined equivalent) scoped to the inner PARALLEL_GATEWAY's own reachable subgraph: resolve the inner split's own branches to their own single agreed inner join, and then -- critically -- treat the WALK AS CONTINUING PAST that inner join's own outgoing edge(s), not treat the inner join itself as branch 1's leaf. Concretely this means: when collect_leaf_gateways/3 reaches a :PARALLEL_GATEWAY node whose in-degree/out-degree (via the same gateway_role/2 classification dispatch_parallel_gateway/4 already uses, transition.ex:730-741) makes it a :split (out_degree > 1) rather than the join the caller is actually searching for, the walk must first resolve that inner split's own matching join (recursively), then continue the outer walk from the inner join's own outgoing edge -- NOT stop and report the inner split's id as a leaf. A :PARALLEL_GATEWAY reached with out_degree <= 1 (i.e. actually a :join or :pass_through node from gateway_role/2's own classification) is unambiguously a real candidate join and should keep today's immediate-terminal behavior unchanged. This also needs new recursion-safety reasoning beyond what §2.2.3's termination proof currently covers -- the proof bounds work by 'no node re-explored once memoized/finished,' but a nested-split resolution nested arbitrarily deep (a PARALLEL_GATEWAY inside a branch of a PARALLEL_GATEWAY inside a branch of...) needs its own termination/complexity argument, likely bounded by nesting depth being finite (graph.ex's own node/edge caps) rather than assumed. CODE-DESIGNER should also decide how a nested split's own :no_matching_join failure should propagate -- does it fail the whole outer branch (treating the branch as dead-ended/ambiguous, i.e. contributing to a non-singleton leaf-set), or is there a distinct error shape worth surfacing separately for debuggability. Design must also add regression fixtures mirroring this diagnosis's two repro graphs (a nested split/join fully inside one branch, reconverging before the outer join) to lib/letflow/design's worked-example section and ultimately to test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs (TEST-DESIGNER's job at Step 4, not this step's).
